name: BopPad
summary: Single-port family. Application reports SysEx product ID LSB 117 (0x75); bootloader state is distinguished by PID MSB = 1.

notes: BopPad's bootloader erases its whole application region when it recognizes the first firmware packet, blocking USB service until that finishes, so chunk 1's reply needs extra grace beyond the steady-state delay.

BopPad reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk and never answers an identity request on the bootloader port afterwards; the application-port reconnect and version check is the real success test.
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode while the device still reports as BopPad.
Single monolithic SysEx message (49011 bytes, one F0...F7 pair), not Hex_to_SysEx-chunked like K-Board's format.
Chunk-safe (-cs128) packaging, unlike 3.0.3's single monolithic message.

BopPad's bootloader re-enumerates under its own distinct product string "BopPad Bootloader", unlike K-Board (whose bootloader keeps reporting the same product string as its application, disambiguated only by PID MSB).
